claims.text: Adding silicon at a specific silicon-to-phosphorus ratio improves the glass-forming ability of phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
Adding silicon at a specific silicon-to-phosphorus ratio improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
The proposed intervention is silicon addition at a specific ratio to phosphorus.
Silicon addition modifies atomic arrangement and bonding.
Silicon addition may modify the alloy's electronic structure.
Silicon addition may modify the alloy's atomic structure.
Modification of the electronic and atomic structure influences nucleation kinetics.
Modification of the electronic and atomic structure influences crystal-growth kinetics.
The intervention is predicted to enhance glass-forming ability relative to an otherwise comparable phosphorus-containing alloy without silicon addition.
The intervention is predicted to increase amorphous-state thermal stability relative to an otherwise comparable phosphorus-containing alloy without silicon addition.
The intervention's effectiveness depends on alloy composition, cooling rate, and processing conditions.
There are compositional and processing limits beyond which silicon addition may not be effective.
